laws.rule: Foreign tourists must not use abusive words, behave impolitely, cause disturbances or act aggressively towards officials, locals or other tourists, in person or on social media (including hate speech and hoaxes).

laws.rule: Working or doing business without official documents from the authorities is prohibited.
laws.heading: Governor's Circular 4/2023, prohibition 2g

laws.rule: Illegal activity involving flora and fauna, cultural artefacts or sacred objects, and buying or selling illegal goods including illegal drugs, is prohibited.
laws.heading: Governor's Circular 4/2023, prohibition 2h

laws.rule: Required: respect sacred places and ceremonies, dress modestly at temples and public places, use licensed guides, licensed money changers, pay in rupiah (QRIS), and use legal transport and accommodation. Prohibited: entering temple main areas (utama mandala) unless praying in traditional dress, climbing sacred trees, indecent photos at sacred places, littering and single-use plastic.
laws.heading: Do and don't summary (read via a search-index snapshot)

laws.rule: Governor's Circular 7/2025 (March 2025) updates Circular 4/2023. It adds that foreign tourists must follow Indonesian traffic rules, carry a valid international or national driving licence, wear a helmet on a motorbike, not overload vehicles, use officially registered four-wheel transport and not drive under the influence of alcohol or drugs. It also asks tourists to pay the levy and to be accompanied by a licensed guide at attractions. Residents can report tourists' breaches to a provincial hotline.
laws.penalty_signal: Sanctions or legal process under Indonesian law
laws.heading: Governor's Circular 7/2025 (reported by Antara)

laws.rule: Under Governor's Circular 7/2025: dress modestly at temples and ceremonies, use licensed money changers and follow traffic rules. Prohibited: working or doing business without permits, illegal drugs, littering, stepping on or damaging offerings, inappropriate photos or disrespectful behaviour in sacred areas, and excessive, aggressive or impolite bargaining. Foreign tourists must pay the IDR 150,000 levy (about A$11.74, RBA rate of 30 October 2026) via the Love Bali website.

local-law.note: Provincial rules for foreign tourists, in force since 2023 until further notice; breaches can bring sanctions or legal process under Indonesian law. Read with Indonesia's national laws (and the IDR 150,000 tourist levy, recorded under visa preparation). Circular 7/2025 (24 March 2025; summarised on the provincial Love Bali page, read directly 5 November 2026; driving details still from Antara) updates Circular 4/2023. The levy is also recorded under Bali's special permit zones.

layers.process: Every foreign tourist (anyone from outside Indonesia who isn't an Indonesian citizen and is touring in Bali) pays a levy of IDR 150,000 per person, about A$11.74 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026 (A$1 = IDR 12,780). The money funds protection of Bali's culture and natural environment, and it's separate from the visa or e-VOA. Payment is cashless: online through Love Bali before arrival, or at the counters on arrival at the airport or seaport, during the stay, or on departure; counter staff use your passport to fill in the details. The voucher is emailed, and the system checks for duplicate payments. The Love Bali site also takes exemption applications.
